title: Virgin Galactic wants your help naming its new Delta class spaceship
gist: Virgin Galactic opened public voting through August 27 on four names for its first Delta-class spaceship — Horizon, Explorer, Ascend or Apeiron — while CEO Michael Colglazier put commercial service at February 2027 with flight tests starting in October and a second ship joining in March, a fleet the company claims can fly up to eight missions a month versus SpaceShipTwo's twelve-times-lower rate.

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic claims Delta-class ships may fly as many as eight space missions per month — twelve times what was possible with SpaceShipTwo — thanks to streamlined manufacturing and maintenance.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Flight rate is the entire economic case for suborbital tourism; a claimed 12x cadence improvement is the number to test against actual 2027 operations.
insights.quote: Delta-class ships may fly as many as eight space missions per month, 12 times what was possible with SpaceShipTwo, according to Virgin Galactic.

insights.claim: SpaceShipTwo carried Richard Branson and 31 other people on just 12 short hops above the US-defined boundary of space across its entire operational life, establishing the extremely low baseline the Delta fleet must beat.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: 32 customers over the program's history is the historical revenue reality — the gap between that and eight flights a month is the whole investment thesis.

insights.claim: Delta spaceships are designed to fly with up to six people, the same capacity as SpaceShipTwo, meaning all revenue growth must come from flight frequency rather than seats per flight.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: With capacity fixed, turnaround time is the single operational lever determining whether Virgin Galactic ever reaches profitability.
insights.locator: Like SpaceShipTwo, Delta spaceships are designed to fly

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Colglazier said on August 12 that the first Delta ship is now expected to enter commercial service in February 2027, with the flight test phase commencing in October 2026 and a second spaceship joining the fleet in March.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: October flight test start is the near-term verifiable milestone; slipping it would push the February 2027 revenue date out with it.
insights.quote: We expect to commence the flight test phase with this vehicle in October, with our second spaceship planned to join the fleet in March.
insights.locator: Virgin Galactic plans to debut the Delta spaceship's livery

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic completed structural assembly of Delta-1 earlier in 2026 and towed it from its assembly hangar to a test and launch hangar in Arizona in March 2026, with livery and name debut as the next milestone before delivery to Spaceport America in New Mexico.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Hardware exists and has moved between facilities — a concrete progress marker distinguishing this cycle from earlier Virgin Galactic announcements.
insights.locator: Virgin Galactic completed structural assembly of “Delta-1,”

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic canceled development of VSS Inspire, the second SpaceShip III, in 2024 in favor of the Delta-class design, abandoning the modular SpaceShip III line after only VSS Imagine was built.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: A full program cancellation two years ago explains the current gap in operational vehicles and the sunk cost behind the Delta bet.
insights.locator: VSS Inspire was also announced as the next SpaceShip III

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic narrowed 276 name submissions from teammates and 'Future Astronauts' to four finalists — Horizon, Explorer, Ascend and Apeiron — with public voting open through August 27 to everyone aged 13 and up.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: A low-cost engagement campaign that builds an email and interest list ahead of ticket sales — customer acquisition dressed as participation.

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic explicitly frames the naming vote as a chance for the public to shape spaceflight history and encourages participants to share it with friends and family, positioning the campaign as viral marketing rather than governance.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Consumer-brand marketing tactics applied to spaceflight signal Virgin Galactic is competing for discretionary luxury spend, not aerospace contracts.
insights.quote: Cast your vote, share it with friends and family, and join us as we take another step toward opening space to more people than ever before.

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic uses the term 'Future Astronauts' for clients who have reserved seats, a designation that converts an unfulfilled backlog into a branded community.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Naming your undelivered backlog is a retention tactic for a company whose customers have waited years — watch for deposit refund pressure if 2027 slips.

insights.claim: The first SpaceShipTwo, christened VSS Enterprise in 2009, was lost on October 31, 2014 during its fourth powered test flight, killing co-pilot Michael Alsbury and severely injuring pilot Peter Siebold.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: A fatal in-flight loss during powered testing is the historical base rate that should frame risk assessment of the October 2026 Delta flight test campaign.
insights.locator: Tragically, the VSS (Virgin spaceship) Enterprise was lost

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic returned to flight and reached space for the first time on its second SpaceShipTwo, VSS Unity, which was named in response to messages of support following the fatal Enterprise crash — including one from Stephen Hawking, who had planned to fly.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: The company has recovered from a fatal accident once before, which is relevant precedent for how it would handle another test-campaign setback.
insights.quote: We are entering a new space age and I hope this will help to create a new unity
insights.locator: One of those messages was from astrophysicist Stephen Hawking

insights.claim: VSS Imagine, debuted in March 2021 as the first SpaceShip III with modular construction to ease servicing and mirror-like livery, was originally intended to succeed SpaceShipTwo before the Delta pivot.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Serviceability-driven design has been Virgin Galactic's stated goal across two successive vehicle generations without yet delivering high cadence.
insights.locator: In March 2021, four months before Unity lifted off
